title: Trump Touts Record Crime Drop on Long Island, Backs Blakeman for New York Governor
excerpt: The president released FBI data showing historic crime declines at an event in Nassau County, home to roughly 50,000 Indian Americans and FBI Director Kash Patel's hometown.
body:
• President Trump visited Nassau County, Long Island to unveil FBI data showing the largest year-over-year decline in violent crime on record
  • Trump endorsed Republican Bruce Blakeman for New York governor, who has defied the state's sanctuary policies and partnered with ICE
  • FBI Director Kash Patel, an Indian American who grew up in Garden City, Long Island, joined the event alongside Attorney General Todd Blanche
  • Nassau County is home to roughly 50,000 Indian Americans, making immigration and public safety policies directly relevant to the diaspora

President Donald Trump traveled to Long Island on Friday to release new FBI crime data and rally behind Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman, framing the visit around law enforcement and immigration in a county that has become a political battleground ahead of November's midterm elections.

Speaking at the Nassau County Police Academy in Garden City, Trump unveiled 2025 FBI statistics showing the largest single-year drop in violent crime ever recorded. Murder and non-negligent manslaughter fell an estimated 18.1%, while robberies declined 18.5%, according to an excerpt of the report shared by the White House.

"President Trump promised to make America safe again and the data proves he has done just that."

— Lauren Bis, White House Spokeswoman

Crime Data and Its Contested Origins

Trump credited his administration's mass deportation campaign for the decline, telling the audience, "We're getting them the hell out." But the data tells a more nuanced story. Homicide rates had already been plummeting in 2023 and 2024 to pre-pandemic lows, well before Trump returned to office, according to Reuters. Some violent crimes, including homicides, had surged during the COVID-19 pandemic at the tail end of his first term.

https://x.com/FoxNews/status/2088351497348366782

"This is a case in which success truly has a thousand fathers, not just one," said Adam Gelb, president and CEO of the Council on Criminal Justice. "Everybody is looking for a single easy explanation and that doesn't exist."

Blakeman, Hochul, and the Governor's Race

The visit doubled as a campaign boost for Blakeman, Nassau County's executive, who is challenging incumbent Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul. A recent Siena University poll found Hochul's lead among likely voters had narrowed from 20 points in June to 10 points, though her favorability rating held at 46% compared to Blakeman's 33%.

Blakeman has positioned himself as a staunch Trump ally on immigration, defying recently approved sanctuary state measures pushed by Albany Democrats that ban cooperation agreements between local governments and ICE. Nassau County remains an active partner with federal immigration enforcement, and Blakeman vowed in May to maintain that relationship after visiting Trump at the White House.

Indian American Presence on Long Island

The event carries particular significance for the Indian American community in Nassau County. FBI Director Kash Patel, who joined Trump at the event, grew up in Garden City — the same Long Island town that hosted Friday's speech. Patel, the son of Gujarati Indian immigrants, has become one of the most prominent Indian Americans in the federal government.

Nassau County is home to approximately 50,000 Indian Americans, part of a rapidly growing Asian population that surged 39% between 2010 and 2019. Hicksville, with its thriving Little India corridor and an 18.7% Asian Indian population, has emerged as a cultural hub. Communities in Herricks (23.5% Indian), Manhasset Hills (28.4%), and Garden City Park (18.4%) reflect the growing South Asian footprint across the county.

For these communities, the debate over sanctuary policies, ICE cooperation, and immigration enforcement is not abstract. Many Indian American families on Long Island navigated the H-1B visa system and lengthy green card backlogs to establish themselves in these suburbs. Public safety and immigration policy are interwoven concerns in a region where South Asian residents are both deeply invested in community security and attuned to the complexities of federal enforcement.

What's Next

Trump's Long Island visit signals that New York's governor's race will be a national focal point heading into the midterms. Republicans are betting that crime and immigration can overcome voter frustration over inflation and the economic fallout from the war with Iran, while Democrats argue the crime decline predates Trump and that aggressive immigration enforcement has made some communities less safe. For Nassau County's diverse electorate, including its substantial Indian American population, the stakes extend beyond partisan politics.
